thread:
inc-bot: [ALERT] Incident detected: runtime-prod-1 high GPU memory pressure -> OOM events spike (node group runtime-gpu-1). auto-escalate to pager.

oncall-alex: taking this. pinging SRE + runtime.

support-lena: multiple customer reports of embedding failures and elevated generation latency. 3 customers reported errors since 11:42 UTC. attaching ticket IDs: #4521, #4522, #4523

sre-maya: looking at metrics - memory.used jumps +40% in 2m at 11:41. memory fragmentation visible. linking quick graphs: https://grafana.redwood/runtime-prod-1?panel=mem_usage :eyes:

eng-runtime-chris: getting logs now. current KV cache size for model gpt-large-v1 spiking to ~24GB across shards. suspect KV cache not evicting properly on cold path.

eng-ml-jordan: could be interplay between batch size and KV caching. any recent model or runtime tuning pushed?

oncall-alex: no model rollout in last 24h. we did push batch-sizing tweak to autoscaler at 10:30 UTC yesterday (adjusted max_batch). double-checking config.

eng-runtime-chris: quick log excerpt:
```
2026-03-17T11:41:22Z runtime ERROR alloc 512MB failed on /dev/gpu0: out of memory
KVCache.size = 24576000000
batch_size = 128
eviction_policy = LRU
```

sre-maya: nvidia-smi dump shows GPU mem allocated ~31.2GB/32GB at peak on several workers. fragmentation counters incrementing; lots of small allocations from attention/kv ops.

eng-runtime-chris: propose immediate mitigations: reduce per-request max_batch & cap batch_size to 8 on runtime-prod-1 pool; disable long_kv_cache flag as temporary. anyone object?

pm-omar: customer impact is high; do whatever reduces error rate quickly. keep me posted on rollback risk.

support-lena: applying temporary routing change to reduce batch sizes now, will update tickets and notify affected customers.

oncall-alex: executed config patch: route-limit batch_size=8 on pool runtime-prod-1 at 11:46 UTC. patch id cfg-7892.

eng-ml-jordan: also recommend turning off long_kv_cache for generation requests with prefix >64 tokens as hotfix to limit KV growth.

eng-runtime-chris: applying hotfix: disable long_kv_cache flag on pool; rolling restart of 6/12 nodes to pick up change (11:47-11:49).

sre-maya: observing memory drop; OOM events reduced to 0 in last 3 mins. p95 latency improved from 2.9s -> 1.1s. continuing to monitor.

support-lena: customers #4521 and #4522 confirmed decreased errors. #4523 still intermittent but trending better.

oncall-alex: quick timeline so far:
- 11:41 alert: OOM surge on runtime-prod-1
- 11:42 initial triage (memory graphs + logs)
- 11:44 hypothesis: KV cache eviction lag + batch interaction
- 11:46 mitigation: batch cap -> 8 (cfg-7892)
- 11:47 mitigation: disable long_kv_cache + rolling restart
- 11:50 observed stabilization (OOMs drop, latencies improve)

Keep links to logs and graphs in this thread for RCA.

eng-runtime-chris: uploaded full log dump and kernel traces: gs://redwood-incident-logs/1747654321/runtime-prod-1/logs.tar.gz

sre-maya: capturing heap snapshots + allocator fragmentation metrics; adding to incident timeline doc: https://docs.redwood/incidents/1747654321/timeline

eng-ml-jordan: hypothesis list for RCA (short):
1) KV cache growth due to unbounded per-request prefixes combined with high concurrency -> LRU thrash
2) Allocator fragmentation from many small attention buffers and quantized kernels causing unusable free memory despite aggregate free pool
3) Batch amplification: sudden traffic pattern increases effective memory per step
Please collect: per-request KV delta, allocator free-list counts, batch composition histograms, kernel allocation sizes.

oncall-alex: owners assigned for RCA: eng-runtime-chris (runtime & kernel traces), sre-maya (infra metrics & fragmentation), eng-ml-jordan (kvcache + model interaction), support-lena (customer comms). moving to postmortem channel after stabilization.

pm-omar: include customer impact table and timeline for commercial follow-up.

sre-maya: action items to track: evaluate eviction_policy tuning (LRU -> LFU-ish), consider padding/sizing strategy for small allocations to reduce fragmentation, add fragmentation counters to alerted dashboards, and add KV cap per-request.

eng-runtime-chris: posted short action checklist to thread: reduce default batch, add per-request KV cap, implement eviction quick-path, add fragmentation metrics to alert rules.

support-lena: closing loop: two customers restored, third is flaky but improving. will escalate immediately if regressions.

oncall-alex: thanks all — tagging for RCA follow-up @eng-runtime-chris @sre-maya @eng-ml-jordan @support-lena. moving to incidents-postmortem for write-up. :white_check_mark:
